key: If the age was unsuitable and their mission at failure, they fell back upon their own resources and waited.
s: The chapter says the retired scholars did not hide but met an unsuited age; Guo Xiang, on chapter 16, reads the waiting as a sage’s calm in a busy age: deep-rooted, he waits for things to act of themselves, so the Way is not lost.
src: Guo Xiang, Zhuangzi zhu, chapter 16, zh.wikisource (Nanhua zhenjing zhushu, juan 18, Zhengtong Daozang), revision 6365330 (2026)

evidence.words: 雖有事之世，而聖人未始不澹漠也，故深根寧極而待其自為耳，斯道之所以不喪也。
evidence.gloss: Even in an age given to affairs, the sage is never other than calm and still; so he roots himself deep, rests in the utmost, and waits for things to act of themselves; this is how the Way is not lost.
